name: Present Perfect (førnutid med "har/er")
explanation: Use 'har' + a past participle to ask or talk about whether something has ever happened, without saying exactly when. This is the natural way to ask about someone's experiences in Danish: 'Har du prøvet...?' (Have you tried...?). To answer that you have no experience with something, use 'Jeg har aldrig...' (I have never...).

examples.danish: Har du prøvet at spise sushi?
Jeg har aldrig besøgt et museum i Aarhus.
examples.english: I have never visited a museum in Aarhus.

name: Modal Verbs (kan, skal, vil, må, bør)
explanation: Modal verbs are followed directly by an infinitive without 'at'. Use 'burde' (should / ought to) to give personal advice, and 'kan' together with the general subject 'man' (one / you in general) to make a recommendation that applies to anyone, not just the person you're talking to.

examples.danish: Du burde prøve den nye restaurant.
examples.english: You should try the new restaurant.

examples.danish: Man kan sagtens gå til koncerten uden at booke på forhånd.
examples.english: One can easily go to the concert without booking in advance.
